0.value:
sampler_osc~ treats a recording as an oscillator: a sound file played  under the control of signals.

Click 'load' to choose a file, or send a file path to 'path' (a bang there  opens the chooser too). The file is remembered with the patch. When it  loads, the 'length' outlet sends its duration in seconds.

THE MODES:
They differ in what moves the playhead.

loop      plays round the loop window, with a short crossfade across the 
          seam so the join does not click
oneshot   plays once through the window, then stops. 'start' or the 
          trigger inlet plays it again
scrub     the playhead sits wherever 'position' says, like a record moved 
          by hand. Held still it outputs a steady value, as a stopped 
          record would
follow    'position' is a target the playhead chases on a spring, so 
          movement becomes playback speed: the material sounds while the 
          control moves, and is quiet when it stops. The one for effort 
          data
granular  short overlapping grains, taken from around 'position'

SPEED AND PITCH:
In loop, oneshot and granular, playback speed is 'rate' (a plain  multiplier: 2 is twice as fast) times 'pitch' in octaves, exactly as on  vco~ - so the same envelope or LFO that sweeps a vco~ sweeps this the same  way. In granular they set each grain's speed and pitch while the grains  keep their place, so pitch and position are independent. scrub and follow  ignore both: there 'position' alone moves the playhead.

POSITION AND THE WINDOW:
'loop start' and 'loop end' choose a window within the file, as fractions  from 0 (the start) to 1 (the end). 'position' runs 0 to 1 across that window.

The demo is the classic scan: the file's length sets phasor~'s period, so  its 0 to 1 ramp sweeps the scrub position through the whole file at its  natural speed. Change phasor~'s period by hand from there and the speed  and pitch change together, like tape.

SYNTAX:
sampler_osc~ <path> <mode>

EXAMPLE:
sampler_osc~ granular

INPUTS and PARAMETERS:

rate / pitch:
Speed as a multiplier, and transposition in octaves. Defaults 1 and 0.

position:
0 to 1 across the loop window. Used by scrub, follow and granular.

loop start / loop end:
The window, as fractions of the file. Defaults 0 and 1.

grain size / grain rate / jitter (granular):
Grain length in seconds (default 0.08), grains per second (default 20),  and how far, as a fraction of the window, each grain may land from  'position' at random (default 0).

trigger:
A signal; each rising edge past 0.5 restarts from the start of the window  (from its end, playing backwards).

mode, load, path, start:
The mode; open a file chooser; load a file by path; restart.

enable:
Off fades out over a few milliseconds, then stops computing; the playhead  waits where it was.

OPTIONS:
reverse plays backwards. In oneshot the playhead starts at the end of the  window and runs back to the start, then stops; a negative 'rate' does the  same.
loop crossfade is the seam's fade in seconds (default 0.005); scrub also  uses it to smooth over jumps in position.
follow speed is how quickly follow mode's spring catches up (default 8).

OUTPUTS: 

left out / right out:
The signal. A mono file comes out of both.

length:
The loaded file's duration in seconds, sent when it loads.

RELATED:
phasor~ is the ramp for scanning position.
polyphonic_sampler~ and granular_sampler~ are the other sample players.
